stemBlocks.value: P, Q, R and S lie on a circle with centre O; RP is a diameter and AB is a tangent at P. Angle APQ = 3x°, angle QPR = 2x°, angle RPS = x°, and angle QSP = 54°. Determine, with reasons: (i) the value of x, (ii) angle y = angle PRS, (iii) angle z = angle PQS.
Think first: The tangent and the diameter meet at P at a right angle, and that single fact turns the labelled angles into an equation in x.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p245-q11 from workbook page 245.

solutionSteps.instruction: Use the right angle between the tangent AB and the diameter RP at P.
Write down the angles at P that this gives.
Use the angle in a semicircle at S in triangle PRS.

contentBlocks.value: RP is a diameter, so ∠RSP = 90°; then y = 180 − 90 − ∠RPS = 180 − 90 − 18

solutionSteps.instruction: Find z from the angle sum of triangle PQS.

contentBlocks.value: ∠QSP = 54° and ∠QPS = 54°, so z = 180 − 54 − 54 (equivalently z = ∠PRS = 72°, angles in the same segment on chord PS)

strategyBlocks.value: Add the angles between the tangent and the diameter to make 90° and solve for x, use the semicircle right angle at S to get y, then use the triangle PQS (or angles in the same segment) to get z.

finalAnswerBlocks.value: (i) x = 18 (tangent perpendicular to the diameter at P gives 3x + 2x = 90)  (ii) y = 72° (angle in a semicircle ∠RSP = 90°, then angle sum of triangle PRS)  (iii) z = 72° (angle sum of triangle PQS, or equally ∠PQS = ∠PRS as angles in the same segment on chord PS)

whyThisWorks.value: Because the radius OP is perpendicular to the tangent, everything on the tangent side of P is measured from a right angle, which is what makes 3x + 2x = 90 legitimate. The diameter RP then forces a right angle at S, since any angle subtended by a diameter from the circumference is 90°. Finally, PS is a chord seen from Q and from R on the same side of it, so those two angles must be equal — a check that the 72° is right.

commonErrors.misconception: Using 3x + 2x + x = 90 by including ∠RPS, which lies on the other side of the diameter.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Using 3x + 2x + x = 90 by including ∠RPS, which lies on the other side of the diameter.

commonErrors.misconception: Setting the angles at P equal to 180° without noticing which of them make the right angle.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Setting the angles at P equal to 180° without noticing which of them make the right angle.

commonErrors.misconception: Assuming ∠QSP = 54° is the angle in the alternate segment for 3x without checking which chord it stands on.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Assuming ∠QSP = 54° is the angle in the alternate segment for 3x without checking which chord it stands on.

commonErrors.misconception: Confusing the angle at the centre with the angle at the circumference.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Confusing the angle at the centre with the angle at the circumference.

examTip.value: Mark the 90° at the point of contact and at the end of any diameter before you start — most of these questions unlock from those two right angles.
